abstract:
Bone development, homeostasis, and regeneration are governed by complex, dynamic gene regulatory programs, and these processes are disrupted in numerous skeletal diseases. The epigenetic landscape-particularly chromatin accessibility-dictates transcription factor binding and gene expression, which fundamentally shape bone cell fate and function. In recent years, single-cell chromatin accessibility technologies, most notably single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq), have revolutionized bone epigenome research and enabled single-cell resolution dissection of the skeletal system.
This review summarizes recent progress in single-cell chromatin accessibility studies in bone biology, and systematically outlines chromatin-accessibility changes in skeletal development, diseases, and regeneration. We introduce cutting-edge single-cell epigenomic mapping technologies, their bone tissue-specific adaptations, and analytical frameworks for multi-omics data integration.
These approaches reveal key biological findings: the identification of bone-resident subpopulations and lineage hierarchies, dynamic enhancer landscapes during osteoblast/chondrocyte differentiation, cellular bases of diseases such as osteoporosis and osteoarthritis, and novel mechanisms of bone tumorigenesis. Moreover, we discuss cross-applications of genomics and functional research, including mapping of disease-associated regulatory elements and emerging epigenome-editing strategies. Finally, we address current challenges, outline future directions, and envision the integration of single-cell epigenomics in precision orthopedics and regenerative medicine.
